children: Bell Potter analyst Michael Ardrey is waiting for a shift in sentiment or further visibility on a recovery in job volumes before becoming more positive on Australian job advertiser Seek. Ardrey tells clients in a note that there are some positive signs, with Seek's proprietary ad volume index slowing its annual rate of decline in September. On top of that, he thinks potential near-term monetization of assets in Seek's growth fund offers asymmetric upside risk. However, Ardrey warns that rising interest rates could be a headwind when it comes to achieving exit prices. Bell Potter maintains a hold rating and lifts its target price by 4.6% to 13.60 Australian dollars. Shares are down 2.0% at A$12.82. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
